# Release Notes - awake 0.5.0-beta

Release date: 2026-10-22 Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The fifth beta release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps the system awake. This release adds a first-run license agreement, an elevation warning and a section-aware configuration parser.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project is generated by AI and has not been extensively reviewed. Please scrutinize the code carefully before use. The author is not responsible or liable for any consequences arising from the use of this software.

## Highlights

- **First-run license agreement**: the client embeds the full Apache License 2.0 text and shows it on the first run together with the official page URL, then asks `[y/N]`. Accepting stores `license_accepted = true` in `awake.ini` and the question never appears again. `awake help` and `awake version` work without accepting. A non-interactive stdin (redirected input, pipes, CI) is treated as a refusal, so scripts never hang.
- **Elevation warning**: running `awake` or `awake.daemon.exe` from an administrator console prints one yellow warning line. Such a daemon cannot be stopped or contacted from a normal shell, which used to look like "the process runs but does not respond". The warning never blocks the command. `awake status` reports an elevated daemon as `Daemon: running (elevated)` (the GET_STATUS response gained an `ELEVATED=0|1` line).
- **Section-aware configuration**: `awake.ini` now understands sections. Only `[watch]` (and files without any section header, as written by older versions) contribute watch entries; other sections hold `key = value` settings and are never mistaken for image names. This is what makes the new `[license]` section possible.
- **Smoke test grown to 52 checks**, including the license gate (blocked command, embedded text, official URL, non-interactive refusal, `help`/`version` exemption, reset clearing the flag) plus two new manual checklist items for the elevation warning and the license prompt.

## Behaviour changes

- The first run after upgrading asks for the license once, because `awake.ini` written by older versions has no `[license]` section. This is expected.
- `awake reset` restores the initial template and therefore clears `license_accepted`; the next command asks again.
- Duplicate watch entries are still rejected, and the `awake add` / `awake del` behaviour is unchanged. If the end of the file is not in the `[watch]` section, `awake add` now appends a `[watch]` header first so the entry is read as a watch entry.

## Full command list

```
awake help              Show the help message (with version).
awake version           Show the version.
awake 0                 Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                 Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake status            Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                        watch list status.
awake screen on         Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                        and idle lock).
awake screen off        Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on         Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off        Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable     Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable    Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake reload            Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset             Reset the configuration file (asks for
                        confirmation).
awake add <imagename>   Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>   Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

See the command aliases note in `awake help` for the shorthand forms.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool. The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on first use; the first command also asks for the license.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only; after a daemon restart they are inactive again.
- The daemon sends a one-shot stay-awake notification when it starts, regardless of the current settings.
- If you enabled autostart and later move the executables to another folder, `awake status` will flag the stale entry and `awake daemon enable` in the new location fixes it.
- Avoid running the tool from an elevated console: the warning explains why, and `awake status` flags an elevated daemon.
- This is a beta release; the behavior and the command line interface may still change in incompatible ways before 1.0.
